Subject: Revised order form and a few clarifying asks

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are our redlines to the Order Form (named HelioTech_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf). A couple of high-level items our procurement team wants clarified before we can route to finance:

- Invoicing entity: we need invoices issued to HelioTech US Inc (EIN 12-3456789) rather than your international entity — can you confirm your billing entity and whether you can invoice that US entity?
- Pricing cadence: the schedule in Appendix A shows monthly tiered true-ups. Can Redwood commit to a calendar-month invoice and a single aggregated monthly invoice by customer entity?
- Minimum commit: we propose splitting the annual minimum into quarterly tranches (25% per quarter) — please confirm if that will affect pricing bands or ramp credits.
- Net terms: HelioTech prefers Net 45 for vendor onboarding. Is Net 45 acceptable, or can you confirm Net 30?
- VAT / Withholding: if any withholding applies, we will provide certificates, but we need to know what evidence Redwood requires.

We’re trying to close this before our fiscal cut-off on 12/20. Marcus and I are on standby for a short call if it’s easier.

Thanks,
Sophie Lane
Procurement Manager, HelioTech

Hi Sophie — thanks for the redlines and the clear list. Looping in Ben (Sales) and Kimberly (Legal/Billing) so we can run through each ask and get a consolidated response.

Quick answers up front:
- Invoicing entity: need to confirm with Billing; we often invoice from Redwood Inc (US) and can support US entity invoicing in most cases.
- Monthly aggregated invoice by entity: sounds reasonable; Ben, can you confirm operationally?
- Quarterly tranche for min commit: that’s typically acceptable, but pricing bands can be impacted if the annual guaranteed volume materially changes — will look with Legal.
- Net terms: we can discuss Net 45 for first-year onboarding; Kimberly, what’s the legal/billing stance here?
- VAT/withholding evidence: Kimberly — what certificates do we need from the customer?

If helpful, I’m available tomorrow 9–11 PT for a quick 20-minute call to finalize.

Thanks —
David Kim

Hi all,

Thanks — I reviewed HelioTech's redlines and the items David flagged. Summary and recommended positions below so the sales team knows what to commit to: 

1) Invoicing entity
- We can issue invoices from Redwood Inc (US) to HelioTech US Inc; we’ll need the customer PO and the remit-to details. If HelioTech needs invoices from a different Redwood entity for tax reasons, we should flag with Finance and confirm whether that requires an intercompany arrangement.

2) Monthly aggregated invoice
- Acceptable: Redwood can produce a single calendar-month aggregated invoice per customer entity, showing line-item detail for usage/true-ups. Operationally, we will need the billing contact and PO format to ensure matching.

3) Minimum commit tranching (quarterly)
- A quarterly tranche (25%/quarter) is acceptable. Legal note: if pricing bands are tied to annualized committed volume, splitting by quarter should not change the tier definitions so long as the annual minimum remains the same. If HelioTech expects tiered discounts to apply earlier, we can add a ramp credit clause to protect them during the initial quarters.

4) Net terms
- Standard Redwood position is Net 30. For enterprise onboarding we can offer Net 45 for the first 6 months pending credit approval. If HelioTech requires Net 45 as a hard term, we will need Finance sign-off and potentially a short credit assessment.

5) VAT / withholding evidence
- If withholding is applied by HelioTech, we require an official withholding certificate from the local tax authority and a completed W-8/W-9 as relevant. If reverse-charge VAT is claimed, provide the relevant VAT registration and a statement referencing the applicable law.

Action items:
- David / Ben: confirm whether you want to propose Net 45 trial for 6 months or push for Net 30.
- Ben: once Sophie confirms the PO and remit details, send to billing@redwoodinference.com (cc Kimberly) so Finance can confirm entity routing.
- I’m attaching a clean Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with language for ramp credits and a Net 45 trial option — please review and run by HelioTech.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / David — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clean form. HelioTech can accept the following today:

- Invoice to: HelioTech US Inc (EIN 12-3456789). We will supply PO HT-2026-9812 and remit-to details in the next email.
- Monthly aggregated invoice per entity is confirmed.
- Minimum commit: quarterly tranches (25%) accepted without changing the annualized tiers; we appreciate the ramp credit language — please include in the final Order Form.
- Net terms: HelioTech accepts the Net 45 trial for six months as proposed. After six months we will re-evaluate payment terms.
- VAT/withholding: we will provide any withholding certificates required. If Redwood can list required documents in the invoice cover note, that will help our finance team match payments.

We have a short internal sign-off today and will route the PO to you by EOD tomorrow. If you can send the final Order Form with the ramp credit and Net 45 trial clause inserted, we can execute.

Best,
Marcus Reed
Head of Procurement, HelioTech
